final_candidates.decision_summary: N171Y (N501Y in full Spike) forms key pi-stacking and hydrogen bond contacts with human ACE2 Y41 and K353, driving significant receptor affinity enhancement.
Q168R (Q498R in full Spike) introduces an electrostatic salt bridge/hydrogen-bonding network with ACE2 D38 and Q42, markedly boosting binding kinetics.
L122R (L452R in full Spike) enhances localized hydrophobic packing and backbone stability in the receptor-binding motif while promoting high ACE2 affinity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations are backed by extensive experimental DMS literature and structural evidence for ACE2 binding enhancement; further computational queries will not alter rankings.

history.rationale: Corresponds to N501Y in standard SARS-CoV-2 numbering, which significantly increases ACE2 affinity through pi-stacking and hydrogen bonding with ACE2 Y41 and K353.
Retained from initial candidate pool prior to gathering tool evidence. N171Y aligns with key RBD contact modifications that enhance ACE2 affinity.
N171Y (N501Y) is the gold-standard affinity-enhancing mutation for SARS-CoV-2 RBD binding to human ACE2. Moderate ESM-1v score is outweighed by established experimental literature.
Corresponds to Q498R in standard numbering, forming additional salt bridges/electrostatic interactions with human ACE2 residues D38 and Q42.
Retained from initial candidate pool; introduces favorable electrostatic interaction at the ACE2 binding interface.
Q168R (Q498R) establishes key electrostatic contacts with ACE2 and shows near-maximal ESM-1v plausibility (0.994). It remains a top candidate for enhanced ACE2 affinity.
Corresponds to Q493R in standard numbering, establishing new salt bridge interactions with ACE2 E35 to enhance binding affinity.
Retained from initial candidate pool; basic substitution at position 163 forms additional contact network with ACE2.
Q163R (Q493R) achieved a 1.000 ESM-1v likelihood score and forms favorable hydrogen bonds/salt bridges at the ACE2 interface.
Corresponds to S477N in standard numbering, stabilizing the flexible receptor binding loop and increasing contact with ACE2.
Retained from initial pool; modifies local loop conformation to favor receptor interaction.
S147N (S477N) is well-tolerated in the flexible loop region but exhibits slightly lower ESM-1v likelihood compared to top candidates.
Corresponds to T478K in standard numbering, increasing positive surface potential near the ACE2 binding interface.
Retained from initial pool; lysine insertion enhances electrostatics near the receptor-binding ridge.
T148K (T478K) shows evolutionary presence in MSA (frequency 0.33) and moderate ESM-1v support.
Corresponds to L452R in standard numbering, enhancing receptor interaction while remaining structurally compatible.
Retained from initial candidate pool pending evolutionary and language model validation.
L122R (L452R) scored a perfect 1.000 in ESM-1v plausibility and is known to enhance both RBD stability and ACE2 receptor binding. Reranked into the Top-3.
Corresponds to L455F in standard numbering, optimizing hydrophobic packing at the ACE2 contact boundary.
Retained from initial pool; aromatic substitution aims to improve core packing and binding site stability.
L125F (L455F) enhances localized hydrophobic interactions with ACE2 while retaining solid language model plausibility.
Corresponds to N439K in standard numbering, forming a novel salt bridge with ACE2 E329.
Retained from initial candidate pool prior to biological tool assessment.
N109K (N439K) demonstrates positive ESM-1v score (0.784) and forms a favorable interaction with ACE2, but ranks below top interface drivers.
Corresponds to E484K in standard numbering, altering surface charge and maintaining tight binding to ACE2.
Retained from initial pool; charge reversal at position 154 targets complementary ACE2 residues.
E154K (E484K) displays a maximum ESM-1v plausibility score (1.000) and preserves robust ACE2 binding affinity.
Corresponds to F486L in standard numbering, providing favorable hydrophobic interactions with ACE2 leucine/methionine hydrophobic pocket.
Retained from initial pool pending plausibility and conservation checks.
F156L (F486L) scored 1.000 on ESM-1v and 0.50 in MSA coverage, indicating high structural tolerance.
